children: on Wednesday surged to a 24-year high above 5.30%, surpassing its previous 2007 peak.

The benchmark yield spiked to as high as 5.31% (+5 basis points) in afternoon trading, reaching levels unseen since the spring of 2002, in the face of resilient U.S. economic data combined with ongoing concerns about energy-driven inflation and mounting fiscal debt.
That leaves the 10-year note some 55 bps for the month and 138 bps higher than its March 2026 low.
The broader Treasury curve is climbing alongside it, with 2-year
yields rising to 4.89% (+2 bps), 5.10% (+4 bps), and 5.65% (+8 bps), respectively, all hovering around multi-year highs.
Still, policy-sensitive short-dated yields didn't rise as much as long-dated ones at press time as
of a Federal Reserve interest rate increase at the Oct. 28–29 Federal Open Market Committee meeting fell sharply after a softer-than-expected PCE inflation report.

title: U.S. 10-year Treasury yield crosses 5.30% to highest since 2002
